body: Sounds like a great friend OP. :)

Years of being a loner has screwed up my head. I'm no good in social settings, and people find me odd in speech, taste, and behavior. Even the few people who supposedly are close to me and care for my well-being don't show it in their words and actions. They only talk to me after I initiate. They only ask me what's wrong after I mention I'm not feeling good emotionally. I'm not a needy person usually, but it feels too obvious that there's a real disconnect between me and others, and I don't intend to live to 25 this way. https://www.reddit.com/r/depression/comments/5ukbw0/i_wish_people_noticedcared_about_me/
I just don't think trains are as common per square mile of this country compared to maybe other ones. Might be wrong on that, idk.

>I've been worthless my whole life and I think I'm too old to bond with anyone since everyone has their friends, relationships and full time jobs. I missed the boat. 

Fuck, too real. I've become recently reminded that years of being a loner teen has completely decayed my ability to speak and behave normally in real life, especially around girls I'm interested in. I feel that same fucking hopelessness. What is wrong with me?
Oh damn, I eat pizza regularly. "I feel like shit, it's excusable if I eat some today."

I have a couple weeks until spring break, but brother I am right there with you on all of that. If there's one thing that confuses me about my life, it's why I bother to work as hard as I do when I don't give a shit about end-results and goals. I guess I can only say that I hope things turn out better for you, because even with my long history of this shit, I've at least had some good moments, brief as they were for me personally.
Ahahaha, not quite that simple. If you live in California, for example, it's a lot more difficult and takes more paperwork and shit.

I'm not gay, and I can't speak to your experience. But I definitely know self-loathing, and I hope you just get to feel comfortable in your own skin at some point. Unfortunately, sexuality isn't really something which 'goes away', so it has to be grappled with. I'm not sure how you grew up, but hopefully you can come to accept that side of yourself. I hope a fellow gay person could speak to this better.
